body: Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon is Konami's Nintendo 64 action adventure about preventing the Peach Mountain Shoguns from transforming Japan into a giant theatrical production. Goemon travels with Ebisumaru, Sasuke and Yae through towns, open country and dungeons, switching between companions to use their different abilities. Traditional imagery sits beside machinery, sudden musical performances and deliberately absurd humour. The journey makes the group's personalities part of its geography: a place that stops one traveller may be crossed by another who has learned the right technique.

Ebisumaru can shrink to pass through small openings, while the other companions bring their own weapons and special movements. Training challenges introduce abilities that open further routes, encouraging the player to connect a new skill with a place seen earlier. Towns provide conversation, equipment and a pause between expeditions. Their inhabitants give the adventure a social rhythm alongside its platforming and fighting. Moving onward involves understanding what a companion can do as well as learning where the next important destination lies.

Major confrontations place the player inside the enormous Impact robot, shifting the view and controls for a much larger fight. Those sequences and the extravagant songs make the adventure's changes of tone part of its identity. Released in Japan in 1997 and overseas in 1998, it introduced many Western players to a broader version of Goemon's world. The game treats its setting as a place where everyday travel, supernatural abilities and giant machinery can belong to the same expedition without losing the comic company at its centre.
